description.value: The H.R. MacMillan Space Centre, also known as the Planetarium, has been British Columbia's premier space science attraction since 1968, situated in Vanier Park on the waterfront just off the popular Vancouver seawall cycling route. It offers an immersive full-dome planetarium theatre, hands-on exhibits featuring moon rocks and meteorites, and live science demonstrations. Cycling visitors exploring the Kitsilano and Vanier Park area will find it a natural cultural detour.

bike_parking_detail: 2 racks within 100m: stands (8 spaces) at 22m; stands (12 spaces) at 77m. Total: 20 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website fully corroborates the OSM record: address (1100 Chestnut Street, Vancouver BC V6J 3J9), phone ((604) 738-7827), and website URL all match. The site confirms the venue is actively operating with ticketed programming. No mention of bike parking, washrooms, café, water refill, or any cycling-specific amenities appears anywhere in the website content, so those fields remain null per the evidence rules. Notably, the OSM tag 'fee=no' directly contradicts the website, which lists explicit paid admission prices — this discrepancy is flagged in concerns.
concerns: OSM tag 'fee=no' is incorrect — the website clearly lists paid admission prices for all age categories. The OSM record should be corrected to 'fee=yes'.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A well-established, actively operating cultural attraction on Vancouver's waterfront seawall cycling corridor; touring cyclists exploring Vanier Park would benefit from this listing.

wow_evidence: BC's premier planetarium/space science centre since 1968; full-dome theatre, moon rocks.
